title: Top Salary In The Company
description:
Report the single highest salary in the company.

Name the column `top_salary`. The result is exactly one row (NULL if there are no employees).
solutionSql: SELECT MAX(salary) AS top_salary FROM employees;
hint: A bare aggregate always returns exactly one row, even with no data — which is why MAX beats ORDER BY ... LIMIT 1 here.
outputExplanation: The highest salary in the company is $150,000.

title: How Many Of Each Title
description:
Report each job title and the number of employees holding it, but only for titles held by **two or more** people.

Name the columns `title` and `headcount`. Return the result in any order.
solutionSql:
SELECT title, COUNT(*) AS headcount
FROM employees
GROUP BY title
HAVING COUNT(*) >= 2;
hint: Filtering on an aggregate is HAVING, not WHERE.
outputExplanation: Three employees are Engineers, two are Managers, and two are Reps. Analyst is held by only one person and is not reported.

title: Departments In Austin
description:
Report the `name` of every department located in Austin.

Name the column `name`. Return the result in any order.
solutionSql: SELECT name FROM departments WHERE location = 'Austin';
hint: Straight equality filter on the departments table alone.
outputExplanation: Engineering and HR are located in Austin. Sales is in Denver.

title: Salary Range Per Title
description:
For each job title report the lowest and highest salary paid.

Name the columns `title`, `min_salary` and `max_salary`. Return the result in any order.
hint: Two aggregates over the same GROUP BY.
outputExplanation: Manager salaries range from $130k to $150k, Engineers from $95k to $120k, Reps from $70k to $85k, and the single Analyst earns $60k.
